record.summary: Bipartisan House bill on frontier AI models, trained with more than 10^26 operations. All frontier developers would publish transparency reports on new models and report critical safety incidents within 72 hours. Larger developers, tiered by revenue and AI spending, would also publish frontier AI frameworks, register, undergo annual independent audits and report catastrophic risk; the largest would retain a licensed independent verifier. A new Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security would administer it, the Commerce Secretary could suspend models posing imminent catastrophic risk, and new state catastrophic-risk transparency, audit and incident-reporting rules would be preempted.
record.notes: Introduced on 23 Jul 2026 by Rep. Jay Obernolte with Reps. Lori Trahan, Scott Franklin, Scott Peters, Erin Houchin and Suhas Subramanyam; the bill text published with the announcement leaves the bill number and the committee blank. The sponsors say it was developed as part of their broader Great American AI Act framework. Large frontier developers have AI-related development expenditures of at least $1B and revenues above $50M; very large ones at least $10B and above $5B, measured over 36 months. Preemption (Sec. 9) is aimed at state frontier-safety statutes such as California SB 53, New York's RAISE Act and Illinois SB 315, and preserves generally applicable laws, use- and deployment-based rules for deployers and users, laws protecting minors, and state procurement and use rules. Civil penalties reach $1M per violation per day, and $10M per violation per day for emergency orders, whose wilful violation is criminal. Rules on minimum framework requirements, licensing of independent verification organisations and modification criteria are due within 180 days of enactment. On 1 Oct 2026 Reps. Obernolte and Trahan said the bill would build on the White House Accord that leading AI companies had signed and make it durable.

summary.quote: The term "frontier model" means a foundation model trained using more than 10²⁶ operations
It further requires all frontier developers to publish, before or when deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model, a transparency report

(h) DISCOVERY OF A CRITICAL SAFETY INCIDENT.— 10 (1) I N GENERAL .—Subject to subsection (g) 11 and except as provided in paragraph (2), not later 12 than 72 hours after a frontier developer learns facts
and to undergo an annual independent compliance audit and register with the Under Secretary
requires large frontier developers to also report catastrophic risk arising from their models, including internal use
It requires each very large frontier developer to retain an IVO for ongoing assessment

This section authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to suspend or restrict a frontier developer's development, deployment, or internal use of a frontier model upon a written finding that it presents an imminent catastrophic risk.

it prohibits any State or political subdivision from imposing new substantive obligations on AI developers as to frontier AI catastrophic-risk transparency, third-party auditing and independent verification, or incident reporting

notes.quote: The bipartisan legislation, which was developed as part of the broader Great American AI Act framework
gross revenues above $50M plus at least $1B in such expenditures for the large tier, and gross revenues above $5B plus at least $10B in such expenditures for the very large tier
The clause is aimed at closely related State frontier-safety statutes (e.g., CA SB-53, NY RAISE, IL SB-315).
Violations carry a civil penalty of up to $10M per violation per day, and willful violations are criminal.

It places three rulemakings on 180-day clocks: minimum requirements for frontier AI frameworks; IVO licensing and oversight; and criteria for substantial (model) and material (framework) modifications.
